# Quiet

> Quiet is a free, browser-based classroom noise monitor for the projector or interactive whiteboard. It shows a calm savanna, coral reef, woodland clearing, rainforest jungle, Arctic sea ice or prehistoric floodplain where shy animals come out the longer the room stays quiet, or, for older students, deep space, where a telescope picks up satellites, comets and galaxies. There is no sign-up, no ads and nothing to install, and microphone audio is measured on the computer and never recorded or sent anywhere.

Quiet is the opposite of a bouncing noise meter: there is no needle and no red warning light. The teacher sets a volume goal (Silent, Independent or Partner work, or anything in between) and presses Start. The first animal appears after 10 to 20 quiet seconds, then about one every few minutes of quiet work (Relaxed, Normal or Lively, or a custom number of minutes). Brief noises such as a knock at the door do not count. When the room stays too loud, the scene clouds over and, by default, animals run away; teachers can instead choose to pause the scene so nothing is taken away. The savanna has 17 animals, the coral reef 18, deep space 17 sightings, the prehistoric scene 17 animals, the forest 17 animals, the jungle 17 animals and the Arctic 17 animals, in common, uncommon and rare tiers. In deep space, noise shows up as interference, and sightings fade into static rather than run away. It is available in English, Spanish and French, and works in Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari on laptops, Chromebooks and interactive whiteboards.

Classes can also compete in the Class Cup: each class scores the share of its session time the room spent under the line, and the board tells every class how much more time under the line it needs to take first place. A class's animals, notes and Cup score are kept separately on the teacher's computer.

Quiet came out of the EdTech-a-thon and is maintained by teacher.dev. It is free, with no paywalls, no ads and no tracking of personal data.

- [How it works](https://qui-et.pages.dev/#how-it-works): what it does, how to use it in class, how it decides the room is too loud, and answers to common questions
- [Privacy](https://qui-et.pages.dev/privacy): what is and is not collected
